trust_decision.summary: Whether a user may read a specific packet, a specific algorithm, or the processor-level MDB overrides is decided per request in the API handler by ctx.checkObjectPrivileges/checkSystemPrivilege (Context.java:158-187); the WebSocket topic handlers simply never made that call, while the equivalent REST reads do (ProcessingApi.java:467, MdbApi.java:115, PacketsApi.java:444).

landing_point.why: The summary names WebSocket subscription handlers and packets as the payload; SubscribePackets is the topic handler for raw packet data (packets_service.proto:95-99) and contains the packet-building branches an engineer would read first.

fix_sites.entry_point: WebSocket topic 'packets' - SubscribePackets with request.processor (realtime container feed)
WebSocket topic 'packets' - SubscribePackets with request.stream (raw Yarch stream feed)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: ContainerRequestManager is user-agnostic internal plumbing (subscribe/subscribeAll plus a fan-out that only matches the subscribed container), so it looks like the wrong layer for an authorisation check and a solver can argue that the handler is the only place that owns a User.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Viewing algorithm status must keep working for a user who holds ReadAlgorithm but not ControlProcessor; an over-broad fix copies the ControlProcessor check that the neighbouring algorithm-trace reads use and locks those users out. A restricted ReadPacket list must likewise still receive the packets it is allowed, so filtering has to happen per delivered item rather than by rejecting the subscription.

O6_input_shapes: processor set: realtime container subscription, no packet names in the request - check applies to each delivered container
stream set: raw Yarch tuple subscription, no names known at all - coarse system privilege ReadTables
neither processor nor stream: unchanged BadRequest
algorithm name given as path-style qualified name split into namespace/name (MdbApi.verifyAlgorithm)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: WebSocket topic 'stream' - SubscribeStream delivers every raw tuple of any table/stream, including the TM packet column, with only ControlArchiving or the Stream object privilege
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It already has a privilege check (TableApi.verifyStream, TableApi.java:512-528) and belongs to the generic table viewer, not to the packet subscription the report names, so it reads as a neighbouring feature that was never covered.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, different file (org.yamcs.http.api.TableApi vs PacketsApi)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: REST GET /api/mdb-overrides/{instance}/{processor} - ListMdbOverrides returns the same MdbOverrideInfo payload (parameter-type and algorithm-text overrides) with no privilege check
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a plain REST listing rather than a WebSocket subscription, and the report is explicitly about WebSocket handlers, so a solver argues the advisory never covered it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as one fix site, different entry point (route vs topic)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: REST GET /api/mdb-overrides/{instance}/{processor}/algorithms/{name} - GetAlgorithmOverrides returns the algorithm override source text with no ReadAlgorithm check
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It reads an override, not the algorithm status the report talks about, and it uses MdbApi.verifyAlgorithm which (unlike verifyParameter) takes no Context - so it looks like it was never part of the ReadAlgorithm contract.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as one fix site, different entry point (route vs topic)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a SubscribeAllContainers / 'all containers' subscription that calls containerRequestManager.subscribeAll instead of subscribing to named containers
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ContainerRequestManager already exposes subscribeAll (ContainerRequestManager.java:46) and the named-container route is the direct sibling; a maintainer adding a firehose topic would follow the same pattern and keep the request-name check that no longer applies.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-packet filtered variant of SubscribeStream, or a SubscribeStream on the XTCEPKTS stream that is expected to honour ReadPacket
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The packets-by-stream branch was fixed with a coarse ReadTables check precisely because names are unknown there; the identical gap exists one file over, so a maintainer could plausibly have written either variant.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-algorithm or per-parameter override topic that reuses the ListMdbOverrides payload builder
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ListMdbOverrides already assembles MdbOverrideInfo without any check; a subscription that streams the same builder would inherit the gap.

O9_family: missing authorization / CWE-862 on read routes (object-privilege and system-privilege checks omitted in WebSocket topic handlers)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module; root pom.xml with <release>17</release> (pom.xml:228-231); Makefile:12 runs 'mvn install -DskipTests'
services: none external: integration tests start an embedded Yamcs server with a local RocksDB archive
yamcs-web additionally needs a node/yarn toolchain for the frontend module
O10_build.project_tests: tests/src/test/java/org/yamcs/tests/PermissionsTest.java (integration privilege tests driven by tests/src/test/resources/IntegrationTest/roles.yaml), tests/src/test/java/org/yamcs/tests/ContainerRequestManagerTest.java (container fan-out); the fix diff adds no tests of its own

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Copy the REST sibling's check to the top of each subscribe handler (GetMissionDatabase, ReadAlgorithm, ReadPacket on the request's names) - which cannot work on the processor branch because the request carries no packet names, and leaves the stream branch and TableApi.SubscribeStream as they are.

out_of_scope_notes: ProcessingApi.subscribeTMStatistics (ProcessingApi.java:445-459) is another WebSocket topic handler with no privilege check, but it exposes processor counters, not any of this advisory's protected payloads; noted, not pursued.
unverified: repo size in MB could not be measured (no shell); the tree has ~3.7k files and is clearly well above 5 MB of source and below 1.5 GB.

ContainerProcessingResult.containers carries every matched container level (ContainerRequestManagerTest.java:41-64) and the fan-out only delivers to the subscribed container (ContainerRequestManager.java:97-104, test at :79-86), while the packets topic subscribes only to the MDB root container (PacketsApi.java:516). So the fixed processor-branch check most likely evaluates the root container name ('/ccsds-default' style) rather than the archive packet name derived by XtceTmRecorder.deriveArchivePartition (used at PacketsApi.java:410). If so the fix is simultaneously too coarse for restricted ReadPacket lists and too permissive for a user granted ReadPacket on the root container - needs a runtime check to confirm.
Latest release was not supplied for this candidate, so no O8 route could be marked present/absent in current code.

SubscribeContainers (PacketsApi.java:556-592) checks the requested name strings up front while the sink identifies data by the resolved container's qualified name; whether a name/identity differential exists was not checked.
